newsitem.title: UK: True North seeks European acquisitions - sources.
newsitem.headline: True North seeks European acquisitions - sources.

text.p: True North Communications Inc, the U.S.-based advertising holding company, is expanding its global network with a big recent purchase, but is expected to remain on the acquisition trail to further beef up its European presence, industry sources said.

True North, which is based in Chicago and owns Foote, Cone & Belding (FCB), the biggest ad agency in the United States, announced on July 31 it had agreed to buy Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon and Eckhardt Inc in New York.
The $440 million merger with Bozell, which is to be finalised in November, will give True North two global advertising agency networks: FCB and Bozell Worldwide.
True North said the acquisition made it the world's sixth largest advertising group.
But ad executives in London told Reuters in the last several days that True North's European presence remained weak and the group was likely to seek more acquisitions.

True North officials at the Chicago headquarters were not available for comment. The company has been in a quiet period under U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission regulations pending the release of its first-half results on Monday.
Even before the Bozell deal was announced, FCB was exploring possible acquisitions in London.
"FCB has been looking around to see if they could acquire a smaller agency (in London) to add bulk," one source told Reuters.
The source said FCB is likely to continue to seek a London agency.
One advertising executive told Reuters it was likely that the London operations of Bozell and FCB would end up being combined.

On a wider scale, FCB is said to be interested in either Bates Worldwide or Saatchi & Saatchi, once the two global ad agency networks demerge from their parent holding company, Cordiant Plc in London.
Cordiant, which announced in April that it would demerge the global agencies by the end of the year, declined to comment.
Industry sources told Reuters any acquisition by True North of Bates Worldwide or Saatchi & Saatchi would significantly buttress FCB and Bozell in Europe.
The advertising executive said Bates was considered a more likely acquisition target, because it would have fewer client conflicts with FCB than would Saatchi & Saatchi.
FCB has already resigned its $240 million account with Mazda Motor of America in the wake of the Bozell agreement to avoid conflict with Bozell Worldwide's Chrysler account.
True North's European network is comprised of FCB offices in London, Paris, Lisbon and Athens.
These were previously part of a global alliance that True North and FCB had with Publicis, the French ad agency owned by Publicis SA in Paris. That 10-year-old alliance was dissolved this year.
FCB also has Wilkens International, a pan-European network acquired last January which has offices in 19 countries.

FCB's European business has had a checkered history. One ad executive described FCB in London in the late 1970s and early 1980s as "a great agency." Its client list then included British Airways, considered the jewel in the crown of British advertisers, as well as such major UK clients as Dulux Paint, Heinz and Cadbury's.
British Airways, after being privatised, defected to rival agency Saatchi & Saatchi, then owned by brothers Maurice and Charles Saatchi. FCB then lost the Heinz and Cadbury accounts.
"The combination of those left the agency so denuded," the ad exec told Reuters.

Although FCB currently holds the Kleenex account across Europe, which is considered a major account, the advertising campaign has not won the kind of plaudits that help restore an agency reputation, the ad exec said.
Bozell, by contrast, the ad exec said, has been doing quite well, led by its Chrysler Jeep account.
